candidates.source_summary: It'll be free to attend too
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The Grade I-listed Rochdale Town Hall and gardens will be hosting its popular fire festival once again later this winter and it’ll be free to attend. Built in 1871, the Grade I-listed Rochdale Town Hall is considered by Historic England to be ‘one of the finest municipal buildings in the country'. Just two years ago, the hall reopened following an ambitious restoration, which saw many of its original features repaired and has since been nominated for a number of awards. Earlier this year, Rochdale’s historic Broadfield Park Slopes, which sit between the Town Hall and St Chad’s Church, were also brought back to life with a restored fountain, new accessible pathways and improved landscaping. Click here for the latest on Manchester's food & drink scene, gigs and more in our CityLife newsletter The town hall and its gardens will take centre stage in one of the borough’s biggest winter events with the return of the popular Ignite Fire Festival, which will be held from November 20 to 22. Attended by around 10,000 people last year, the centrepiece of the 2026 event will consist of a light and fire trail featuring six walk-through zones all designed around the theme of the human body. The nighttime event, which will run from 5pm to 8pm across the three days, will mark the North West premiere of the ambitious fire and light installation, which has been created by Walk The Plank and has been shown in the likes of Ireland and Canada so far. Visitors will be able to walk through the ‘glowing embers’ of human metabolism and learn more about what keeps us alive through cutting-edge technology and dramatics. The attraction will also feature a Fire Garden consisting of illuminated slopes and gardens behind the Town Hall that will feature intricate hand-crafted fire sculptures and pyrotechnics. There will also be the 20-strong drumming collective Drum Machine, who will be bringing their lively, stomping tunes to proceedings. In addition, special Fireflies shows featuring mesmerising fire spinning from Rochdale’s Skylight Circus Arts and live fire shows by interactive arts group Travelling Light Circus. Each night, there will also be flame-cooked hot food on offer, as well as mulled wine and other seasonal drinks to enjoy. Councillor Sue Smith, cabinet member for communities and co-operation at Rochdale Borough Council, said: “Ignite Fire Festival has become a real success story for the borough, drawing audiences from across Greater Manchester and beyond. This 2026 line-up will build on that success with new attractions, creative performances and family-friendly experiences. It will be a fantastic celebration for residents and visitors alike, setting the stage perfectly for our Christmas lights switch-on.” Bev Ayre, senior producer at Walk the Plank, added: “The Body is unlike anything we’ve brought to Ignite before. An immersive fire and light experience that combines art, science and creativity to help people discover the incredible human body in a fun and engaging way. “Set against the stunning backdrop of Rochdale Town Hall Square and gardens, it promises to be one of our most exciting attractions yet. candidates.source_summary: Completion of base build marks next phase for Rochdale’s advanced materials and manufacturing innovation hub 30,000 sq. ft centre designed to connect research, specialist facilities and commercial production Development forecast to generate £107m in economic value over 10 years The base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The base build of the Sustainable Materials & Manufacturing Centre (SMMC) at Kingsway Business Park in Rochdale has been completed, marking a major milestone in the development of Atom Valley’s advanced materials and manufacturing innovation district. Designed by Bond Bryan, the 30,000 sq. ft centre will provide a physical gateway into the UK’s advanced materials and manufacturing network, connecting businesses with specialist space, facilities, research expertise and support to help move new technologies from concept towards commercial application. The building is the first major physical development within the Atom Valley Innovation District (AVID), a 25-acre hub in Rochdale intended to bring together businesses, researchers, investors and innovation partners. The next phase will focus on specialist fit-out ahead of the centre becoming operational in 2027. The project addresses a key challenge for advanced manufacturing: creating environments that support the transition from research and development to commercialisation and production, while accommodating specialist processes and allowing for emerging technologies and changing business needs. Mark Adey, director at Bond Bryan, said: “The SMMC is about creating the infrastructure that allows innovation to move beyond the laboratory and into commercialisation and manufacture. That transition places very different demands on a building, so the challenge is creating highly technical environments that work for specialist processes today, while remaining flexible enough to respond to technologies and businesses that are still emerging. “We’ve spent decades designing research, science and advanced manufacturing environments across the UK, and that experience has shown us that the most successful places connect people, ideas and processes rather than treating research and production as separate worlds. SMMC brings those elements together in one place, creating an adaptable environment that can evolve alongside the industries it supports.” Rochdale Development Agency (RDA) has led the physical development of the centre, working with the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA), The University of Manchester and wider innovation partners to secure investment and establish advanced materials and manufacturing as a priority for Rochdale and Greater Manchester. The project builds on the establishment of the Centre of Expertise in Advanced Materials and Sustainability (CEAMS) in 2023. Convened by RDA, CEAMS connects businesses with a national network of specialist expertise, facilities and innovation support, including The University of Manchester, the Henry Royce Institute, the National Physical Laboratory (NPL), the Centre for Process Innovation (CPI) and NCC, formerly the National Composites Centre.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale council's deputy leader was detained by authorities for a 'short period' on arrival in Pakistan, the town hall has confirmed. Councillor Daalat Ali travelled to the country last week as part of a civic delegation. The Kingsway ward representative is touring Sahiwal with Rochdale's ceremonial mayor, councillor Faisal Rana, and others. Members of the delegation have posted pictures on their travels and details of meetings. Last week, social media rumours began to circulate about Coun Ali being detained. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Town hall bosses said Coun Ali is believed to have been held for a 'short period'. "As far as we are aware, this is related to Coun Ali's long-standing personal campaigning in relation to the Kashmir region," a spokesperson added. Coun Ali, they said, is 'safe and well' and has continued on his travels with the party. The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office confirmed a man was detained and released and that the government department was 'in contact with local authorities'. The council's statement reads: "We understand that councillor Daalat Ali was detained by authorities in Pakistan for a short period while travelling as part of a civic delegation from Rochdale . "As far as we are aware, this is related to Coun Ali's long-standing personal campaigning in relation to the Kashmir region and it is not unusual for people who travel to this region to be detained and questioned about their political views. "Coun Ali is safe and well and has since been able to continue travelling with the party and undertake meetings with government officials and dignitaries, as part of the visit’s itinerary." Officials have not confirmed the reason for Coun Ali's detainment. Coun Ali has not responded to requests for comment. The trip is understood to be aimed at strengthening relationships between Rochdale and Punjab city, Sahiwal. The two areas were 'twinned' in 1998, with many Rochdale residents having family roots in the city. Councillors Rana, Ali and others have attended a number of events during the trip, including the opening of the Sewing Machine Centre by the Al-Mahmood Foundation, established by Humanity Care Relief.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area. Rochdale Council refused Caterina Buonocore’s application for retrospective planning permission for the 1.55m high boundary fence — about twice the height of the original — around 19 Town House Road, Littleborough. She appealed that decision. But yesterday, a Planning Inspector rejected the appeal, stating: “The main issue is the effect of the appeal development on the character and appearance of the area. “Boundary treatments in the area are typically low-level and visually permeable, contributing to a sense of openness and allowing the soft landscaping within front gardens to remain appreciable. The existing greenery helps to soften the street scene and makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of the area. “The appeal development introduces a close-boarded timber fence. The height, materials and extensive continuous form of enclosure contrasts with the more open and traditional forms of boundary treatment typically found in the locality. “On site, I observed that due to the prominent corner location, when seen from Park View against the back drop of traditional stone terraces with low-key forms of boundary treatment, the appeal development appears particularly stark and incongruous within the street scene. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Barry Jones was standing in the road when both drivers failed to stop Police have seized a car and a moped after their drivers failed to stop for a lollipop man on two separate occasions, forcing him to leap out of the way. Barry Jones was standing in Bury Old Road in Heywood, Greater Manchester, when the incidents happened on 13 and 14 October, Rochdale Borough Council said. The council said 137 incidents of drivers failing to stop for school crossing patrols had been reported across authority area over the past five years. Greater Manchester Police seized the silver Skoda car and moped after gathering evidence, including witness statements. The law was changed in June to remove the requirement for police to issue a warning before seizing vehicles under the Police Reform Act 2002. Barry Jones pictured helping pedestrians cross Bury Old Road Dylan Williams, cabinet member for highways, thanked police for their "quick and decisive action" and said the council would keep reporting incidents and push for prosecutions where possible.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Rochdale school has closed after a bomb threat earlier today. Greater Manchester Police were called to St Cuthbert’s RC High School which was placed into lockdown this morning following a call made to the school. All students and staff were accounted for and the school has closed for the day. It expects to reopen on Monday as usual. A spokesperson for the school said: “The emergency services were called and all school buildings were evacuated as a precautionary measure. All children and staff are safe and accounted for, in line with our established procedures. “Police attended and parents and carers were notified immediately that their children had been removed to a safe distance and there was no threat or danger to anyone present.” READ MORE: Hundreds object to plans to demolish house and build 45-home development They added that the school building and grounds will be thoroughly checked and reassured parents about speculation on social media. “We’d also urge people to avoid speculation on social media — particularly regarding false rumours, such as any referring to intruders or weapons being present on school premises.”

The operation led to the execution of 20 warrants – mostly in Rochdale and Heywood – as well as in areas across Bury, Salford, Manchester, Merseyside and Yorkshire. candidates.source_body_excerpt: Foster carers who have between them clocked up a total of 465 years supporting children and young people across the borough have been recognised by Rochdale Council. A total of 34 fostering families were honoured at the council’s recent annual Foster Carer Celebration Awards at Rochdale Town Hall in gratitude for their outstanding commitment to providing safe, stable and nurturing homes for some of the most vulnerable. Between all the carers, it is estimated they have supported more than 1,020 children and young people from newborn to 18, while working with the local authority. Among those celebrating their individual milestones was Michael, aged 79, and Marilyn, aged 75, who are marking 50 years. Predominantly caring for newborn babies and siblings since 1976, the married couple from Milnrow have cared for more than 330 children in that time and are still welcoming youngsters into their home. Marilyn said: “We’ve been to their weddings, adoption parties, christenings, 18th and 21st birthday parties. “It’s lovely when you think you started off with them as a baby and now, they’ve grown. Ian and Carole McLean celebrate 40 years of fostering with Rochdale Council “We’ve had letters from adoptive parents saying, ‘They’ve turned out like they have because of you’ which is nice.”

candidates.source_summary: An October 2026 update from Andrew Johnson, Chair of the RBH Representative Body

This recent review looked at how we can encourage customers to provide feedback about our investment programme. You can read more about the review on the RBH website , and I want to say thank you to all the panel members who worked so hard on the review, and also all the RBH team members who took the time to help. Finally, I want to remind you that being a Member of RBH means becoming part of something bigger. It offers you the opportunity to have a real voice in shaping the services we deliver, influencing decisions that affect your home, workplace, and community, and helping RBH continue to improve and grow. If you're not already a member, it only takes a few moments at www.rbh.org.uk/join to sign up, and I encourage you to do so. Membership strengthens our organisation. The building was visited by Principal and CEO Julia Heap OBE, Rochdale Member of Parliament Paul Waugh, the Mayor and Mayoress of Rochdale, Faisal Rana and Iram Faisal, among others. candidates.source_summary: Renovating Rochdale's iconic Seven Sisters tower blocks would force residents out of their homes for more than a decade, housing chiefs have said.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Renovating Rochdale’s iconic Seven Sisters tower blocks would force residents out of their homes for more than a decade, housing chiefs have said. While Rochdale Boroughwide Housing says no decision on the future of the landmark College Bank blocks has been taken, residents have asked new Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig to back their campaign to refurbish their homes rather than demolish them. But if campaigners get their wish, the scale of bringing the 61-year-old buildings up to modern standards would take more than 10 years and they could not be occupied until the work is complete, RBH chiefs have said. Members of Greater Manchester Tenants Union recently met Ms Craig to discuss the steps that could be taken to renovate almost 1,000 homes in College Bank and Lower Falinge. Plans to demolish College Bank were first discussed in 2017 when RBH warned that the buildings were approaching the end of their life. Tenants set up the Save the Seven Sisters campaign and hoped RBH’s partnership with Legal and General Affordable Homes would see the towers restored. But in September, 2024, it was announced that the partnership would not continue. The union and the Save the Seven Sisters campaign asked then Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham to help. In November, 2024, the Mayoral Taskforce was established to look at the options for the College Bank estate. Rochdale’s skyline without the Seven Sisters towers. Image: Copilot In October 2025, RBH announced the results of surveys which found the blocks were not safe to remain occupied and residents would be required to leave their homes.

candidates.source_summary: SPECIAL REPORT: As clutter boxes pile high in the living rooms of the 90 remaining households on Rochdale's College Bank estate, an M.E.N. investigation uncovers BSR building safety notices, £1.7m empty council tax bills, and the human cost of a decade-long housing limbo. George Lythgoe reports.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Claire Lord sits alone in her living room surrounded by head-high boxes. The small space between her sofa and TV is the only bit of the flat not crowded by cubes of clutter. To answer the door she has to clamber over yet more plastic tubs filled to the brim with her worldly possessions. The 56-year-old is ready to move out of her flat in Rochdale ’s iconic Seven Sisters tower blocks. She’s been ready for weeks. Claire was one of 229 households told they had to leave by landowners Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) in October 2025. Since then, droves have been moving out of the blocks. Only an estimated 90 households are still left in Seven Sisters - actually named College Bank. RBH says this has been done for safety reasons. The tower blocks face an uncertain future, with the question of demolition or refurbishment still on the table after a decade of limbo. No matter the decision, it is understood all residents will have to move out whilst work is done - whether that work is to decorate or destroy. Claire is one of the latest to be exiting the estate, but it’s not a move she really wanted to do. When describing the day when RBH told her they'd found some new digs for her, she said she was ‘gutted’. The security, the views, proximity to healthcare professionals and the community are the things she cherishes most about her flat. Claire will be moving to a bungalow across the road, behind Lidl. “There has been a delay because the lady who lived in the bungalow hadn't done work on the place for some time,” Claire explained. “They’ve had to do painting and decorating, rewiring, putting new doors on and a fresh kitchen. “So they’ve been getting it ready for me. RBH told me about four months ago that I’d be moving and were waiting for the date. “Every time I’ve gone down they’ve come up with more work and more work to do. I’ve been down every week to ask. “It’s always the same story - ‘something is being done’. I’ve still not got a move-in date, I think I’ll be told about a move-in date in four weeks. “I do love living here. The security is good and there isn’t much chance of you getting burgled. “It’s close to the shops in the town centre, my mental health team is nearby and my GP is just down the road. “But my biggest fear of moving is losing that security. I’ve been here (in Mardyke block) for 12 years and I've never had any trouble, it’s a good community. “If I could stay I would. It’s not good for my mental health. I don’t know whether I’m coming or going. “Being stuck halfway is no good as I just don’t know. They’re just going to plonk a day on me.” Claire has credited RBH with supporting her through the transition. She has regular contact with housing officers, but that doesn’t mean the transition process has been easy for her. Like many of the tenants, she just wants to know what’s happening with the blocks. Claire added: “We’ve had so many rumours about what is happening. We’ve heard they’re bringing in migrants in; that three are staying up and four are coming down; then we’ve had that they’re all staying up; then we’ve had they’re all coming down and they’re building 250 houses. “Nothing is set in concrete and they won’t tell us. It’s all just rumours.” Her friend Christine Hartley, who has lived in the Tentercroft block for 14 years, hasn’t accepted any new accommodation from RBH. She is still waiting on a 'like for like replacement', which she admits isn’t really possible due to the size of her two-bed flat. The 67-year-old said:

candidates.source_summary: Rochdale mum Sarah Hickman urges women to attend NHS breast screening after a routine mammogram found breast cancer early, before she had any symptoms
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A woman whose breast cancer was discovered through a routine NHS screening appointment is urging others not to ignore their invitations after doctors found the disease before she noticed any symptoms. Sarah Hickman, 50, said she had no concerns about her health when she attended her first routine mammogram after receiving an NHS invitation. However, just one day later she was asked to attend the Breast Unit at Bolton NHS Foundation Trust for further investigations. Following additional imaging, an ultrasound and a biopsy, Sarah was diagnosed with a small breast cancer that had been detected at a very early stage. Recalling the experience, she said: “Mine was a textbook case. "Because I'd turned 50, I'd received my invitation for routine screening and went along without any concerns. "The next day I received a message asking me to come to Bolton for further tests. "It all happened very quickly, but throughout the process I felt completely reassured.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: John Doolan challenged rampant Accrington to push for the play-offs after they cruised to the biggest away win in their Football League history at toothless Rochdale. Josh Woods, Charlie Warren, Tyler Walton – with a brace – and substitute Alex Henderson all struck in a dominant 5-0 victory as Stanley made it nine games in a row unbeaten in all competitions. Remarkably, it was also their first away win since February but it took them up to ninth in League Two. Asked if the play-offs were a genuine incentive for Accy, boss Doolan – whose team finished 16th last term – said: “Yeah, it always has been for us. “We say to the players, you’re trying to progress and develop and be better than last year, and last year at one point, round about February, we were six points off the play-offs. “So to be sitting where we are now, one point off the play-offs, is credit to the players.” Doolan savoured the “outstanding” goals Accy scored as he urged them to build on what he felt was “probably” the best performance of his two-and-a-half-year reign. “A result like that just helps build momentum,” he said. “I think we’ve had that for the past eight, nine games now.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Tyler Walton notched a double as on-song Accrington extended their unbeaten run to nine games in all competitions with an emphatic 5-0 win at Rochdale. The points were all but secured by half-time as John Doolan’s side fired home three impressive strikes before the break on the way to their biggest victory since March 2025. Dale were booed off after a fifth successive match without victory. Stanley grabbed the lead in the 14th minute when Josh Woods guided in a low effort from 20 yards out after home goalkeeper Sam Waller passed the ball straight to him. Walton then slipped a lovely pass through for Charlie Warren to lash a low strike in off the post from the edge of the box in the 38th minute. Walton arced a stunning angled strike over Waller from just inside the box in first-half stoppage time. The winger doubled his tally in the 51st minute when he knocked in the rebound after Joe Anderson’s shot was saved by Waller. Sub Alex Henderson sealed the rout in the 66th minute by finishing off a brilliant move from 10 yards out.
